hint1: An artist transformed pain, identity, and cultural heritage into intensely personal visual symbolism.
hint2: The Mexican painter known for vivid self-portraits, distinctive brows, and a marriage to muralist Diego Rivera.

name: Hedy Lamarr
hint1: A glamorous film star also pursued serious technical ideas far from the movie set.
hint2: The actor who co-invented a frequency-hopping communication system that helped inspire modern wireless technology.

name: Ginger Rogers
hint1: A performer made sophisticated dance partnerships and musical comedy central to her screen legacy.
hint2: The Oscar-winning star who famously danced opposite Fred Astaire in films including Top Hat and Swing Time.

name: Josephine Baker
hint1: A performer crossed the Atlantic to become an international stage sensation while challenging racial barriers.
hint2: The entertainer who became a French Resistance agent, civil rights advocate, and the first Black woman inducted into France's Pantheon.

name: Linda Ronstadt
hint1: A remarkably versatile vocalist moved among rock, country, pop, and traditional Mexican music.
hint2: The singer behind Blue Bayou and You're No Good who also recorded acclaimed albums of standards and mariachi music.

name: Louise Bourgeois
hint1: An artist turned memories, family relationships, and anxiety into psychologically charged forms.
hint2: The creator of the giant spider sculpture Maman, whose work became widely celebrated late in her career.

name: Margaret Mead
hint1: A scholar brought the study of human cultures into public conversation and challenged assumptions about social norms.
hint2: The influential anthropologist who wrote Coming of Age in Samoa and popularized cultural relativism.

name: Nina Simone
hint1: A classically trained pianist fused jazz, blues, gospel, and protest into an unmistakable artistic voice.
hint2: The singer behind Feeling Good and Sinnerman who recorded the civil rights anthem To Be Young, Gifted and Black.

name: Rachel Carson
hint1: A scientist's lucid writing helped awaken the modern environmental movement by making ecological harm impossible to ignore.
hint2: The author of Silent Spring who challenged the widespread use of synthetic pesticides.

name: Rita Hayworth
hint1: A dancer and performer became one of the defining glamour figures of Hollywood's studio era.
hint2: The Gilda star whose performance of Put the Blame on Mame and iconic red hair made her a lasting screen legend.

name: Shirley Temple
hint1: A child performer became a symbol of optimism before later serving her country in public life.
hint2: The star of Bright Eyes and Curly Top who later became a U.S. ambassador to Ghana and Czechoslovakia.

name: Simone de Beauvoir
hint1: A writer and philosopher examined how societies construct gender, freedom, and the roles assigned to women.
hint2: The author of The Second Sex whose existentialist work became foundational to modern feminist thought.

name: Yoko Ono
hint1: An experimental artist worked across performance, music, film, and conceptual art while challenging audience expectations.
hint2: The creator of Cut Piece and a musical collaborator of John Lennon who also pursued a solo recording career.

name: Marlene Dietrich
hint1: A performer cultivated an androgynous, sophisticated persona that made her an international star.
hint2: The star of The Blue Angel who sang Falling in Love Again and entertained Allied troops during World War II.

name: Patti LaBelle
hint1: A vocalist with a dramatic range built a celebrated career in soul, funk, gospel, and pop.
hint2: The Godmother of Soul known for Lady Marmalade, On My Own, and her influential work with Labelle.

name: Gwen Verdon
hint1: A dancer brought electric precision and comic sensuality to some of Broadway's most celebrated musicals.
hint2: The four-time Tony winner who originated roles in Damn Yankees, Sweet Charity, and Chicago.

name: Betty Friedan
hint1: A writer gave language to the frustrations of many women and helped organize a major social movement.
hint2: The author of The Feminine Mystique who co-founded the National Organization for Women.

name: Agnes Varda
hint1: A pioneering filmmaker blended documentary observation with intimate, visually inventive stories.
hint2: The director of Cleo from 5 to 7 and Vagabond who became a central figure of the French New Wave.

name: Annie Leibovitz
hint1: A photographer became renowned for theatrical portraits that turned cultural figures into visual stories.
hint2: The photographer known for iconic portraits of John Lennon, Queen Elizabeth II, and major entertainers for Rolling Stone and Vanity Fair.

name: Barbara McClintock
hint1: A scientist uncovered a surprising form of genetic change while studying the chromosomes of maize.
hint2: She won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering transposable genetic elements, or jumping genes.

name: Beverly Sills
hint1: A coloratura soprano brought operatic virtuosity to a broad public audience and later led major arts institutions.
hint2: The celebrated opera singer who later chaired Lincoln Center and the Metropolitan Opera.

name: Chaka Khan
hint1: A powerhouse vocalist moved from funk-rock beginnings into a celebrated solo career in soul and R&B.
hint2: The singer known for Ain't Nobody, Through the Fire, and the anthem I'm Every Woman.

name: Cicely Tyson
hint1: A performer chose dignified, complex roles that expanded how Black women were represented on screen.
hint2: The star of Sounder and The Autobiography of Miss Jane Pittman who received an honorary Oscar.

name: Coretta Scott King
hint1: A musician and organizer continued a historic movement while building her own powerful legacy of nonviolent activism.
hint2: The widow of Martin Luther King Jr. who founded the King Center and campaigned for a national holiday honoring him.

name: Diana Vreeland
hint1: A formidable tastemaker shaped fashion magazines, designers, and museum exhibitions with vivid editorial vision.
hint2: The former Harper's Bazaar and Vogue editor who later transformed the Costume Institute at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

name: Edith Piaf
hint1: A singer with a dramatic life story turned emotional intensity into a defining sound of French popular music.
hint2: The performer behind La Vie en rose and Non, je ne regrette rien, known worldwide as La Mome Piaf.

name: Fannie Lou Hamer
hint1: A sharecropper became a fearless voice for voting rights after facing violence and intimidation for civic participation.
hint2: She helped found the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party and delivered the powerful testimony beginning 'I question America.'

name: Joan Baez
hint1: A clear-voiced folk performer connected music with pacifism, civil rights, and social justice.
hint2: The singer who performed We Shall Overcome and shared the stage with Bob Dylan during the 1960s folk revival.

name: Leontyne Price
hint1: A pioneering vocalist rose from a segregated Mississippi childhood to international operatic acclaim.
hint2: The first Black American soprano to achieve leading roles at the Metropolitan Opera, celebrated for her Verdi performances.

name: Maya Lin
hint1: An artist and designer uses spare forms and landscape to make history and memory physically present.
hint2: She designed the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., after winning a national competition as a student.

name: Nadia Comaneci
hint1: A teenager transformed expectations for precision and difficulty in international gymnastics.
hint2: She became the first gymnast to receive a perfect Olympic score of 10.0 and won five gold medals across two Games.

name: Nikki Giovanni
hint1: A poet made Black identity, love, family, and resistance central to an influential body of American writing.
hint2: The author of Gemini and Love Poems whose work became closely associated with the Black Arts Movement.

name: Patsy Cline
hint1: A rich, expressive voice helped move country music toward a wider pop audience before her career was cut short.
hint2: The singer behind Crazy, I Fall to Pieces, and Walkin' After Midnight who became a posthumous country legend.

name: Peggy Lee
hint1: A cool, distinctive vocalist moved between jazz, pop songwriting, film, and sophisticated stage performance.
hint2: The singer behind Fever who co-wrote songs for Disney's Lady and the Tramp and recorded Why Don't You Do Right?.

name: Sylvia Plath
hint1: A poet and novelist turned inner experience, mental illness, and domestic life into intensely controlled writing.
hint2: The author of The Bell Jar and Ariel whose work became foundational to confessional poetry.

name: Wangari Maathai
hint1: A scientist connected environmental restoration with women's empowerment, democracy, and community action.
hint2: She founded the Green Belt Movement and became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Wilma Rudolph
hint1: An athlete overcame childhood illness to become one of the fastest and most celebrated competitors of her era.
hint2: She won three gold medals in sprinting at the 1960 Rome Olympics and became known as the fastest woman in the world.

name: Cleopatra
hint1: A multilingual ruler used intelligence, diplomacy, and political alliances to defend an ancient kingdom.
hint2: The last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt who allied with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony before her kingdom fell to Rome.

name: Joan of Arc
hint1: A teenager claimed a sacred mission and became a symbolic leader during a country's existential war.
hint2: The Maid of Orléans helped the French cause during the Hundred Years' War and was later canonized as a saint.

name: Boudica
hint1: A queen turned personal injustice into a massive revolt against an occupying empire.
hint2: The Iceni leader who led a rebellion against Roman rule in Britain and sacked Camulodunum, Londinium, and Verulamium.

name: Hatshepsut
hint1: A royal woman adopted the full authority and imagery of kingship to govern one of the ancient world's great powers.
hint2: One of ancient Egypt's longest-reigning women, remembered for the temple at Deir el-Bahari and prosperous trade expeditions.

name: Nefertiti
hint1: A royal consort became one of antiquity's most recognizable faces through art and religious transformation.
hint2: The Great Royal Wife of Akhenaten whose painted limestone bust became an enduring symbol of ancient Egypt.

name: Sappho
hint1: A poet from an Aegean island made personal emotion, desire, and musical language central to her surviving work.
hint2: The ancient Greek lyric poet whose name gave rise to the term Sapphic and whose fragments remain influential.

name: Hypatia
hint1: A scholar became famous in the ancient world for teaching mathematics, astronomy, and philosophy in a major intellectual center.
hint2: The leading female philosopher and mathematician of late antique Alexandria, remembered as a symbol of intellectual freedom.

name: Marie Antoinette
hint1: A foreign-born royal became a lightning rod for inequality, luxury, and public anger during a political revolution.
hint2: The last queen of France before the French Revolution, remembered for Versailles, extravagant fashion, and her execution.

name: Catherine the Great
hint1: A foreign princess seized power and expanded an empire while presenting herself as a patron of reason and the arts.
hint2: The empress who ruled Russia for more than three decades, expanded its territory, and corresponded with Enlightenment thinkers.

name: Queen Victoria
hint1: A long-reigning monarch lent her name to an era of industrial growth, empire, and strict social conventions.
hint2: The British queen whose 63-year reign shaped the Victorian era and made her a symbolic grandmother of European royalty.

name: Elizabeth I
hint1: A monarch used political skill and carefully crafted public imagery to stabilize a kingdom divided by religion.
hint2: The Virgin Queen whose reign saw the defeat of the Spanish Armada and a flourishing of English theater and exploration.

name: Mary Queen of Scots
hint1: A royal life was shaped by competing claims, religious conflict, imprisonment, and a tragic struggle for legitimacy.
hint2: The Scottish queen who was briefly married to the French dauphin and whose claim to the English throne challenged Elizabeth I.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
hint1: A wealthy heiress became queen in two countries and wielded unusual political influence across medieval Europe.
hint2: The queen consort of Louis VII and Henry II, mother of Richard the Lionheart and John, and a patron of courtly culture.

name: Wu Zetian
hint1: A woman rose through a male-dominated imperial court to claim the highest office in Chinese political life.
hint2: China's only woman to rule as emperor in her own name, she founded the short-lived Zhou dynasty between Tang reigns.

name: Empress Theodora
hint1: A woman from a non-elite background became a powerful partner in governing a vast late antique empire.
hint2: The wife and political adviser of Justinian I who influenced law, religious policy, and the response to the Nika riots.

name: Murasaki Shikibu
hint1: A court writer created psychologically nuanced fiction while observing the rituals and rivalries of aristocratic life.
hint2: The author traditionally credited with The Tale of Genji, often described as the world's first novel.

name: Christine de Pizan
hint1: A widowed writer supported herself through her pen and challenged the contempt directed at women in medieval literature.
hint2: The author of The Book of the City of Ladies, a foundational work defending women's virtue and intellectual ability.

name: Hildegard of Bingen
hint1: A monastic visionary wrote, composed, preached, and studied nature with remarkable authority for her era.
hint2: The Benedictine abbess who composed sacred music, wrote theological works, and was later named a Doctor of the Church.

name: Ada Lovelace
hint1: A mathematically gifted writer imagined that machines could manipulate symbols beyond ordinary arithmetic.
hint2: Her notes on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine included an algorithm often regarded as the first computer program.

name: Jane Austen
hint1: A novelist used wit, romance, and close observation of social class to create enduring portraits of everyday life.
hint2: The author of Pride and Prejudice, Emma, and Sense and Sensibility, whose novels remain central to the English canon.
